entities.summary:
Maternus was a prominent Christian leader who served as the Archbishop of Milan from circa 316 to 328. He played a crucial role in shaping the early Christian Church's stance on faith and morality.

During his tenure, Maternus oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries throughout Italy, establishing a strong foundation for future Christian institutions. His diplomatic efforts helped to secure alliances with various Roman leaders, including Emperor Constantine.

Maternus' legacy extends beyond his own time period, as he was later canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church. His feast day is celebrated on July 18, and he remains an important figure in Christian history.

A striking statistic is that during Maternus' reign, the number of Christians in Milan grew significantly, with estimates suggesting around 10,000 adherents by the end of his term.

A direct attributed quote from Maternus is not available, but his writings on Christian doctrine and ethics have been preserved through various historical sources.

The cultural footprint of Maternus can be seen in the many churches and monasteries he built, which continue to stand as testaments to his enduring legacy.
